bundleNote: A bundle names the ASR model, the speaker embedder and the turn-detection model TOGETHER WITH the diarization operating point that goes with them, so a deployment is never asked for a threshold. The default and every bundle marked redistributable are permissively licensed; a bundle marked redistributable: false carries weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License and is offered only for deployments that accept it. The operating point is a property of the EMBEDDER and the segmentation policy (endpointing silence and the minimum utterance floor), not of the ASR model: the embedding is computed from raw samples, and the ASR model contributes nothing to those samples or, under a fixed endpointing configuration, to where a segment starts and ends. That is why one measured embedder can be paired with a different ASR model without re-measuring - and why a different embedder always needs its own measurement (scripts/calibrate.py).

bundles.name: FastConformer streaming + TitaNet-small (transcription and speaker diarization)
bundles.notes: The default. Threshold placed by the midpoint rule scripts/calibrate.py implements, on TitaNet-small measurements under this bundle's segmentation policy (1200 ms endpointing, 2500 ms minimum utterance). Real meetings: different speakers scored at most 0.107 in one and 0.307 in another (two similar-sounding women), while the same speaker at utterances of 2.5 s and longer scored 0.74-0.91 - midpoint 0.52. Corroborated 2026-09-03 with a synthetic same-gender pair (two male neural TTS voices, 101 s, 81 same/72 different pairs): different max 0.402, same-speaker p5 0.701, recommendation 0.539. The previously shipped 0.4 sat only 0.09 above the hardest real pair and would have merged the synthetic pair's closest utterances; 0.5 clears every observed different-speaker score with margin and stays 0.2 below every observed same-speaker floor. Those measurements were taken with a different (NVIDIA-licensed) ASR model in front of the same embedder; the ASR model does not touch the samples the embedder sees, so the operating point carries over. Status becomes 'vetted' once this exact pairing has been validated on a live multi-speaker meeting.

bundles.name: FastConformer streaming, transcription only (no speaker model in the image)
bundles.notes: Same ASR model, no speaker or turn-detection weights. Transcripts are labelled by audio channel only, exactly as Amazon Transcribe without ShowSpeakerLabel. Pick it for a deployment that never wants per-voice labels and would rather not carry the extra weights in its image; there is nothing to calibrate.

bundles.name: Nemotron 3.5 ASR streaming + TitaNet-small (punctuated multilingual ASR, OpenMDW-1.1)
bundles.notes: Punctuated, cased, multilingual streaming text with the weakest accuracy in the catalog (leaderboard WER 8.72; frequent merged or dropped words in live runs). Prefer parakeet-tdt-v3-titanet-small unless live partial text matters more.

bundles.name: Nemotron speech streaming + TitaNet-small (NVIDIA Open Model License)
bundles.licenceSummary: NVIDIA Open Model License (ASR, not redistributable) + CC-BY-4.0 (speaker) + MIT (segmentation)
bundles.notes: The previous default, kept for deployments that accept the NVIDIA Open Model License. Not redistributable, never the default.

bundles.name: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 offline + TitaNet-small (CC-BY-4.0)
bundles.notes: Default. Vetted live on 2026-09-22: two voices and an advert narrator labelled correctly on every turn of 2.5 s or more, rows within about 20 s of speech, no dropped words. Offline engine: no live partial text while somebody is speaking.

bundles.name: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 offline + TitaNet-small (CC-BY-4.0)
bundles.notes: English-only predecessor of the v3 bundle; same offline engine.

bundles.name: Qwen3-ASR 0.6B offline + TitaNet-small (Apache-2.0)
bundles.notes: Speaker labels are one per utterance: the model returns no word timings, so an utterance holding two speakers is not split. Prefer the FastConformer or Nemotron bundles when per-turn labels matter more than text quality. Memory: the engine peaked at 9.6 GB resident in a two-session, two-minute live run (2026-09-22) on a MicroVM with the 8 GiB minimum, so watch memory on long meetings.

bundles.name: Qwen3-ASR 0.6B offline, transcription only (Apache-2.0)
bundles.notes: Highest transcript quality; rows appear when an utterance closes; labelled by audio channel only.

bundles.name: Cohere Transcribe 2B offline + TitaNet-small (Apache-2.0)
bundles.notes: Not yet run live. Speaker labels are one per utterance (no word timings). Decodes English as baked; set decodeLanguage on the model for another of its 14 languages.

bundles.name: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 offline with a FastConformer live preview + TitaNet-small (CC-BY-4.0)
bundles.licenceSummary: CC-BY-4.0 (ASR) + CC-BY-4.0 (preview ASR) + CC-BY-4.0 (speaker) + MIT (segmentation) + MIT (VAD)
bundles.notes: Two-pass: FastConformer streams a live preview of the open utterance and Parakeet v3 replaces it when the utterance closes. Rows and speaker labels are Parakeet's. Not yet run live.

bundles.name: Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 offline with a Nemotron 3.5 live preview + TitaNet-small (CC-BY-4.0 + OpenMDW-1.1)
bundles.licenceSummary: CC-BY-4.0 (ASR) + OpenMDW-1.1 (preview ASR) + CC-BY-4.0 (speaker) + MIT (segmentation) + MIT (VAD)
bundles.notes: Two-pass with a punctuated, cased preview from Nemotron 3.5; Parakeet v3 replaces it when the utterance closes. Heavier: the preview alone ran at a real-time factor of 0.6-0.9 for one session on a 4-core host, so two sessions per MicroVM may lag. Not yet run live.

models.name: NVIDIA FastConformer streaming English (480ms, int8, CC-BY-4.0)
models.note: The permissive streaming choice: the same cache-aware streaming FastConformer-RNNT architecture as NVIDIA's Nemotron speech model, but CC-BY-4.0 rather than the NVIDIA Open Model License, and a quarter of the download. Trained on NeMo ASRSET - LibriSpeech, Fisher, Switchboard, WSJ, MLS-EN 2000h and Common Voice - so it has seen thousands of hours of spontaneous conversational speech, which is what meeting audio is. Source model exposes 0/480/1040ms lookaheads; 480ms trades a little accuracy for interim text that keeps up with the speaker. English only.

models.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR streaming 0.6B (560ms, int8, OpenMDW-1.1)
models.note: Emits punctuation and casing; multilingual. Live runs on 2026-09-22 showed eight or nine merged or dropped words per two minutes and a real-time factor of 0.6-0.9 for one session on a 4-core host. Open ASR Leaderboard average WER 8.72 (rank 46, 2026-09), the weakest ASR model in this catalog. English validated only.

models.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 offline (int8, CC-BY-4.0)
models.note: OFFLINE, not streaming: it is driven by the accurate engine, which segments audio with Silero VAD and decodes each closed utterance. That trades latency for accuracy - there is no interim text DURING an utterance, only when it ends - so it suits accuracy-first use more than a live meeting view. Chosen over Whisper (also permissive) because TDT is a transducer and reports token timestamps: turn splitting and live cutting both need word timings, and sherpa's Whisper export provides none, which would silently reduce diarization to one speaker per VAD segment.

models.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2 (offline, int8, CC-BY-4.0)
models.note: English-only predecessor of v3; same offline (VAD-segmented) engine.

models.name: Qwen3-ASR 0.6B (offline, int8, Apache-2.0)
models.note: LLM-decoder ASR: the best transcript quality measured here, punctuated and cased, real-time factor 0.38 on a 4-core host. Returns no word timings, so speaker labels are one per utterance. The ONNX export is third-party work re-hosted in the k2-fsa release.

models.name: Cohere Transcribe 03-2026 2B (offline, int8, Apache-2.0)
models.note: Offline 2B model covering 14 languages, decoded in the one language baked from decodeLanguage (it has no language detection). Returns no word timings, so speaker labels are one per utterance. Not yet run live; 2.6 GB of int8 weights, so watch memory. Open ASR Leaderboard average WER 5.40 (rank 7, 2026-09).

speakerModels.name: NVIDIA TitaNet-small speaker embedding (192-dim)
speakerModels.measured: 2026-08-12, native 16 kHz meeting audio: same-speaker cosine median 0.25-0.51 (p5 0.099), different-speaker median -0.02 (p95 0.074, max 0.107). 2026-08-15, a second meeting with 7-20s utterances: same-speaker 0.74-0.91, and two similar-sounding women scored 0.246-0.307 between them while a third, very different voice scored -0.07 to 0.10 against both. Two lessons: same-speaker scores rise sharply once short utterances are filtered out (min_segment_ms), and how far apart two DIFFERENT speakers land depends on the pair - 0.107 for one pair, 0.307 for another - so a threshold has to clear the hardest pair it will meet, not the easiest one it was measured on. 2026-09-03, synthetic same-gender control (two male neural TTS voices, one per channel, 2500 ms floor): same-speaker p5 0.701 / median 0.883, different-speaker median 0.328 / p95 0.376 / max 0.402; utterances under 2.5 s scored 0.09 lower against the same speaker. Midpoint recommendation 0.539; with the real-meeting hard pair (0.307) and long-utterance floor (0.74) the midpoint is 0.52, so the shipped value is 0.5.

speakerModels.name: No speaker model (transcription only, no diarization)

thresholdNote: speakerThreshold is the cosine similarity above which two utterances are treated as the same speaker; higher splits more eagerly, lower merges more eagerly. It is baked into the image from the bundle (model.env) and is deliberately NOT a CloudFormation parameter or a runtime setting: the right value is specific to the embedder and the segmentation policy, and a borrowed or guessed number fragments one speaker into many or merges several into one. To measure a new embedder, run scripts/calibrate.py against a two-channel recording with one speaker per channel and record the result on the speaker model and its bundle.

segmentationModels.name: pyannote segmentation 3.0 (speaker turn and overlap detection)
segmentationModels.note: Converted to ONNX by k2-fsa from the gated pyannote/segmentation-3.0 weights and redistributed ungated with the upstream MIT licence file, so no Hugging Face token is needed. Detects speaker turns and overlap inside one endpointed utterance, which raw embeddings cannot do reliably at short durations.

segmentationModels.name: No turn detection (one speaker per endpointed utterance)

vadModels.name: Silero VAD v5 (utterance segmentation for the offline engine)
vadModels.note: Only the 'accurate' (offline) engine needs this: an offline model cannot stream, so audio is cut into utterances by VAD and each closed utterance is decoded. The v5 export: the runtime feeds its input/state/sr signature.
